text.p: Newspaper publisher Daily Mail & General Trust Plc on Thursday forecast a "satisfactory" year after its first half underlying pre-tax profit rose 27 percent to 46.9 million pounds ($76.6 million).

"Trading conditions in the UK, still the predominant market for the group, remain positive. In these circumstances, the group expects to produce a satisfactory result at the full year," the company said in a statement.

The group said its Associated Newspapers unit produced a satisfactory increase in profit, helped by strong circulation from national titles the Daily Mail and the Mail on Sunday and a 15 percent fall in the cost of newsprint.
The underlying profit figure was towards the bottom of the range of share analysts' forecasts. Exceptional items inflated total pre-tax profit to 65.6 million pounds, against 41 million a year ago.
A one-off gain of 12.4 million pounds was made on the sale of the company's stake in British commercial broadcaster Westcountry Television to Carlton Communications Plc.

The group said it would pay an interim dividend of 7.0 pence per share, up from 4.6p. It said the results justified an interim dividend of only 5.1p but it had raised the payment further to increase the proportion paid at this stage of the year. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
